In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the contingency in the maintenance of operant behavior.
the effects of the contingency between responses and reinforcement on the maintenance and change of behavior.
how the contingency between responses and outcomes influences the rate of response emission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
response-contingency does not affect resistance to change, but stimulus-contingency does.

the results of these experiments are consistent with the hypothesis that response-contingency effects are due to the stimulus-reinforcer relation, but are not due to the relation between response and reinforcer.
the contingency between responses and reinforcers does not affect the resistance to extinction of operant behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of the contingency depends on the schedule of reinforcement and the schedule of nonreinforcers that follows the transition to a richer schedule.
response-contingency effects on resistance to change depend on the nature of the contingency and the nature of the change.
response-contingency effects are not due to the contingency itself, but to the stimulus-reinforcer contingencies that it establishes or maintains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
resistance to change is not a simple function of reinforcement history, but is also influenced by stimulus-reinforcer associations.
the contingency between a response and a stimulus-reinforcer relation is a critical determinant of resistance to change.
the contingency between behavior and reinforcer delivery is not a necessary condition for the maintenance of resistance to change in operant behavior.
